summary: Close a submodule-content integrity gap a guardian-correction review found: a dirty-but-commit-matching mgfembp submodule worktree (locally modified/staged/untracked bytes, even though its own HEAD commit still matched the provenance-pinned commit) could previously be copied live (shutil.copytree) into both independent rebuild materializations and reported verified_success over tampered content. evaluate_rebuild_eligibility() now additionally requires a genuinely clean submodule worktree/index (git status --porcelain, run inside the submodule itself), the submodule's own configured remote URL to agree with .gitmodules's declared URL, and the pinned commit to be a real, locally-accessible object inside the submodule's own object database. Independently, the double-build's submodule-content materializer (_materialize_verified_submodule_content(), replacing _copy_verified_submodule_content()) no longer reads the submodule's live worktree at all -- it extracts the pinned commit's own immutable tree via a second, independent 'git archive <pinned_commit>' run inside the submodule's own repository, exactly mirroring how the superproject's own content is materialized. Publication remains mechanically BLOCKED throughout; the real mgfembp submodule remains uninitialized/unapproved and is never fetched/initialized/approved by this change.
